findings.body: The bind mount source `./.tinysweeper.toml` is a relative path. If this file does not exist on the host when `docker-compose up` is run, Docker will create a *directory* named `.tinysweeper.toml` on the host and mount it as a directory into the container. The container then sees a directory at `/home/tinysweeper/.tinysweeper.toml`, not a file. Depending on how the application reads that path, this can cause a silent fallback to built‑in defaults (the very behaviour the mount was intended to avoid) or an error such as `Is a directory`. The comment states that without the mount the server runs on defaults silently; a mount that accidentally creates a directory reproduces that same silent default behaviour, undermining the fix. Consider verifying that the file exists before starting the service, or use a different mechanism (e.g., a mandatory environment variable pointing to the config, or a volume that always contains a default config).
findings.title: Ensure the config file exists before mounting to avoid directory creation

value.summary: The pull request corrects the GitHub App environment variable names and adds API key environment variables for embedding providers. It also mounts the config file. The change is mostly sound, but the volume mount of `.tinysweeper.toml` uses a relative path that, if the file does not exist, will cause Docker to create a directory instead of a file, potentially leading to silent misconfiguration or errors. This should be addressed before merging to ensure the container always receives a valid config file or fails explicitly when it is missing. No other logic bugs were found in the diff.
